title: Statistics: Mean, Median and Mode of Grouped Data
seo_title: Statistics Class 10 Worksheet with Answers (NCERT Chapter 13)
standard_text: Mean, median and mode of grouped data (bimodal situation to be avoided) (summary of the CBSE syllabus)
meta_desc: Class 10 Statistics worksheet (NCERT Chapter 13): mean by direct, assumed mean and step-deviation methods, mode and median of grouped data, empirical relation. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Mode = l + (f₁ − f₀)/(2f₁ − f₀ − f₂) × h; Median = l + (n/2 − cf)/f × h.
body_html:
How it works

In grouped data each class is represented by its class mark x = (lower limit + upper limit)/2.

Mean = Σfixi/Σfi. With an assumed mean a and class size h: mean = a + h × Σfiui/Σfi, where u = (x − a)/h.

Mode = l + (f₁ − f₀)/(2f₁ − f₀ − f₂) × h (modal class). Median = l + (n/2 − cf)/f × h (median class). Empirical relation: 3 Median = Mode + 2 Mean.

Example

Classes 0–10, 10–20, 20–30 with frequencies 4, 6, 10. Find the mean.

Class marks 5, 15, 25

Σfx = 20 + 90 + 250 = 360, Σf = 20

Answer: 18

Example

Modal class 40–50 with f₁ = 12, f₀ = 7, f₂ = 9. Find the mode.

40 + (12 − 7)/(24 − 7 − 9) × 10

40 + 5/8 × 10

Answer: 46.25

Common mistakes

  • Multiplying the frequencies by the lower limits. Use the class marks.
  • Using f₁ − f₂ on top in the mode formula. It is f₁ − f₀ (the class before).
  • Using the cumulative frequency of the median class itself. cf is the cumulative frequency of the class before it.

faq.q: How do I find the mean of grouped data?
faq.a: Find the class marks xᵢ, multiply by the frequencies, add, and divide by the total frequency: mean = Σfᵢxᵢ/Σfᵢ.

faq.q: What is the formula for the mode of grouped data?
faq.a: Mode = l + (f₁ − f₀)/(2f₁ − f₀ − f₂) × h, where l is the lower limit of the modal class and f₀, f₂ are the frequencies of the classes before and after it.

faq.q: What is the formula for the median of grouped data?
faq.a: Median = l + (n/2 − cf)/f × h, where cf is the cumulative frequency of the class before the median class.

faq.q: What is the empirical relationship between mean, median and mode?
faq.a: 3 Median = Mode + 2 Mean (for moderately skewed data).
